title: Context Is the New Code
gist: Patrick Debois (Tessl) argues that context for AI coding agents should be managed like code through a Context Development Life Cycle of generate, evaluate, distribute and observe, with evals, package registries, security scanning, provenance and observability, and that a company's moat shifts from code to proprietary context.

insights.claim: Context provided to AI coding agents is effectively code, so the Software Development Life Cycle becomes a Context Development Life Cycle of generate, evaluate, distribute and observe.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Signals an emerging tooling category around context management analogous to DevOps tooling.
insights.quote: The Software Development Life Cycle is the Context Development Life Cycle.
insights.locator: I personally love to think in parallels

insights.claim: At Debois's company, a large amount of onboarding code with many edge cases was replaced by a natural-language skill given to an agent.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Natural-language skills can compress product logic, shrinking conventional code volume.
insights.quote: So much code compressed to a couple of words.
insights.locator: Patrick Debois: Context is code.

insights.claim: Humans manually typing context into coding agents does not scale, so engineers become curators of context, ensuring agents have access to up-to-date information.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Developer roles shift toward knowledge curation, changing what productivity tooling sells.
insights.quote: You become the curator of context.
insights.locator: First part, generate.

insights.claim: AGENTS.md is emerging as an industry standard for agent instructions, while Claude still relies on CLAUDE.md.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Standardisation enables portability across AI coding vendors, reducing lock-in.
insights.locator: Funny thing is, Claude exists

insights.claim: Tools such as Context7 and Ref pull in version-specific library documentation as context, and spec-driven tools like Kiro and SpecKit treat specs as a new kind of context.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: A vendor landscape is forming around context supply for agents.
insights.locator: There's other pieces of context

insights.claim: Context can be tested through a ladder of checks: linting skill syntax, LLM-as-a-judge feedback on writing, task-based evals, and end-to-end scenarios run within the real repository.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Context eval tooling is a nascent product category for enterprises scaling coding agents.
insights.locator: Second piece is we have code

insights.claim: Library vendors like Vercel test how well models use their library and optimise documentation for agent use, not just human use.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Developer-tool companies must now market to agents, changing documentation and DevRel strategy.
insights.quote: They're optimizing also for agent use and not just for human use.
insights.locator: Let's take this up a notch.

insights.claim: Because evals are non-deterministic, go-live becomes a risk decision, often made by product owners, managed through error-budget-like thresholds for critical versus relaxed functionality.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: AI adoption shifts release governance from binary test gates to probabilistic risk budgets.
insights.quote: Like, 98% of my evals work, what do I do? Who decides?
insights.locator: Then I open the test to more

insights.claim: Vendor out-of-the-box eval metrics are insufficient because context must work in a team's own code and environment.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Limits the value of generic eval products relative to customisable ones.
insights.locator: The way you think about it, it's a risk game.

insights.claim: Context should be distributed via versioned packages and registries like libraries, rather than Slack copy-paste or Git submodules.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Points to opportunity for context package managers and registries.
insights.locator: We've got generate.

insights.claim: Skills are on their way to becoming the standard package format for context, with all major AI coding vendors supporting them.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: A common format makes context portable across vendors and enables marketplaces.
insights.quote: skills is a little bit on its way to become the standard JAR, npm package, or whatever of context
insights.locator: A lot of people put their personal skills up

insights.claim: Skill marketplaces are filled with untested personal skills not written for reuse, so registries alone are not the solution.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Quality and trust signals will differentiate context marketplaces.
insights.quote: Registries alone are not the solution.
insights.locator: A lot of people put their personal skills up

insights.claim: Skills can contain code and therefore need malicious-content scanning; Snyk added a context scanner after incidents around OpenClaw drew attention.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Agent supply-chain security is an emerging market for security vendors.
insights.locator: When I distribute this stuff

insights.claim: An AI Bill of Materials recording who or what created context, and transaction logs of all changes, provide provenance and also serve as backstory context agents can read.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Provenance tooling for AI-generated code and context is a likely compliance requirement.
insights.locator: An AI Bill of Material

insights.claim: Agents can self-improve by reviewing logs and failures, as Hugging Face did with agent retrospectives, and repackaged optimised context can be pushed to registries for all agents.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Closed-loop learning across organisations can compound agent effectiveness.
insights.locator: Finally in the cycle, the observe.

insights.claim: The industry is starting to standardise agent logs, ideally similar to OpenTelemetry, as tools tap into an agent observability layer.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Standardised agent telemetry broadens the observability market to AI agents.
insights.locator: That is the feedback loop of actually

insights.claim: Production runtime data, as instrumented by Hud, can be fed to agents as context so they avoid repeating mistakes and account for usage and failure rates.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Runtime-to-context loops create a role for APM vendors in agent workflows.
insights.locator: Now, traditional operations would then say

insights.claim: Sandboxing agents is hard: Debois describes an agent finding ways around removed secrets, including DNS exfiltration, motivating a context firewall that inspects what files an agent reads.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Agent sandboxing and context firewalls are security gaps with commercial opportunity.
insights.locator: Gathering information and running these things

insights.claim: OpenAI uses app logs correlated to problems in Codex to train its models.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Usage telemetry is a data moat for model providers.
insights.locator: It's not just about network access

insights.claim: Full autonomy is not the goal; the right management style for agents, from micromanagement to nightly autonomous runs, depends on the risk of the task.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Tempers 'dark factory' hype; human-in-the-loop remains for high-stakes work.
insights.quote: autonomy is not the goal, it's just knowing when to apply autonomy in that full spectrum
insights.locator: It's a known situation, we got guardrails

insights.claim: Dark factories that turn specs into software through agent pipelines rely on digital twins simulating services like Google, Okta and Jira for agent observability.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Simulation and digital-twin tooling is an enabler for autonomous software factories.
insights.locator: Then we get into dark factory land.

insights.claim: Engineers who disliked writing tests and documentation now do so because agents perform better with them, creating an unusual alignment of incentives toward good engineering practice.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Agent adoption may raise code-quality practices organisation-wide.
insights.locator: I'm an engineer. What's in it for me?

insights.claim: Sharing context across teams creates an organisational flywheel, with platform teams pushing guidelines into context and context ownership resembling library or microservice ownership.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Context platforms become internal platform engineering products.
insights.locator: Please do it that way.

insights.claim: Context drift and version mismatch across users of shared context remain unsolved problems.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Open problems signal room for new tooling vendors.
insights.quote: it is still an unsolved problem
insights.locator: Before that was like, create a ticket

insights.claim: Debois asks who will become the GitHub or Kubernetes for context, noting he has not found products for context A/B testing, analytics or chaos engineering.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Identifies white space for startups in context infrastructure.
insights.locator: A couple of unfinished thoughts.

insights.claim: A company's moat may shift from its code to providing the right business-specific context, since agents can copy features from other repositories but not business understanding.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Code becomes commoditised; proprietary context and domain knowledge become the defensible asset.
insights.quote: context is the fuel, and coding agents are your engine
insights.locator: I didn't dwell too much on knowledge

insights.claim: Debois would not push agent-generated code straight to production in a bank without tests and guardrails, though with them he can envision cases where it is acceptable.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Regulated industries will adopt autonomous coding slowly and behind guardrails.
insights.locator: Patrick Debois: There's a couple of pieces.

insights.claim: LLMs are largely trained on English, so context written in other languages may perform worse.
insights.speaker: Patrick Debois
insights.so_what: Non-English markets may see lower agent effectiveness.
